_description: State-level patient protections and billing regulations. Reference only — never cite as legal authority. Always recommend consulting a licensed attorney.
_disclaimer: Esta información es EDUCATIVA únicamente. No constituye asesoría legal.

CA.name: California
protections: Hospital Fair Pricing Act — hospitals must offer financial assistance to uninsured and underinsured patients earning up to 400% FPL
No Surprises Act (federal) applies to all emergency services
Balance billing prohibited for in-network hospital emergency services
Itemized bill must be provided upon request within 30 days
CA.key_agency: Department of Health Care Access and Information (HCAI)

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 4 years (written contracts). Clock starts from last payment or service date. After 4 years, providers cannot sue but may still contact you. CA also has a 12-month limit for debt collectors to file lawsuits under recent medical debt protections.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline for initial billing. Providers should bill within a reasonable time (typically 30-90 days).
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review after internal appeal denial.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: 240 days from first bill (CA Hospital Fair Pricing Act).
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill to initiate Independent Dispute Resolution under federal No Surprises Act.
dispute_deadlines.credit_reporting: As of January 1, 2025, medical debt CANNOT be reported to credit agencies in California. If reported, the debt becomes void.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided within 30 days of request.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: NUNCA haga un pago parcial o promesa de pago por escrito en una deuda antigua sin consultar a un abogado — puede reiniciar el plazo de prescripción.

TX.name: Texas
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Texas Balance Billing Law (SB 1264) — protects against surprise bills in emergencies and at in-network facilities
Itemized bill available upon request
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 4 years (written contracts). Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: 10 MONTHS from service date (Tex. Health & Safety Code §146.002-003). If provider misses this deadline, they CANNOT collect from you or your family. This is one of the strongest billing deadline protections in the U.S.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: Varies by hospital. Nonprofit hospitals must provide charity care per IRS 501(r).
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Hospitals must provide written itemized bill within 30 days of receiving payment. Providers cannot pursue collections until this is provided.
dispute_deadlines.unconscionable_pricing: Freestanding ERs cannot charge more than 200% of average local hospital ER rates for similar services.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: En Texas, si el proveedor no le factura dentro de 10 meses, no pueden cobrarle. Revise la fecha de servicio. NUNCA haga pagos parciales en deudas viejas sin asesoría legal.

FL.name: Florida
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Florida Patient Protection Act — requires price transparency from hospitals
Itemized bill must be provided upon request
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
FL.key_agency: Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA)

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 5 years (written contracts). Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: Doctors have up to 5 years to bill. Insurance contracts may impose shorter deadlines (typically 90 days). Old charges can surface years later — always review past bills.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: Varies by hospital. Nonprofit hospitals must provide charity care per IRS 501(r).
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided upon request — clear, itemized, with explanation of charges in plain language (Fla. Stat. §381.026).
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: En Florida los médicos tienen hasta 5 AÑOS para facturar. Pueden aparecer cobros de años anteriores. Siempre revise la fecha de servicio.

AZ.name: Arizona
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Arizona Surprise Billing Law requires dispute resolution for out-of-network bills
Itemized bill available upon request
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
Medical Debt Relief Program (Prop 209, 2022) — interest rate cap on medical debt
AZ.key_agency: Arizona Department of Insurance and Financial Institutions

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 6 years (written contracts). Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline for initial billing. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: Varies by hospital. AZ also has the nation's largest medical debt relief program (Undue Medical Debt partnership) for patients under 400% FPL.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.prop_209: Arizona Proposition 209 (2022) caps interest rates on medical debt. Application varies by court.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: Prop 209 limita los intereses en deudas médicas. Consulte a un abogado si tiene deudas médicas viejas en AZ — las cortes aplican la ley de forma inconsistente.

NY.name: New York
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
New York Surprise Bill Law — comprehensive protections including independent dispute resolution
Hospital Financial Assistance Law — mandatory charity care for patients under 300% FPL
Itemized bill must be provided upon request
NY.key_agency: New York State Department of Financial Services

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 3 years for medical debt (N.Y. CPLR §213-b — medical debt aligns with consumer debt). This is one of the SHORTEST statutes in the U.S. for medical bills.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: Under NY Hospital Financial Assistance Law, hospitals must provide charity care for patients under 300% FPL (some up to 400%).
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution under NY Surprise Bill Law (which predates and exceeds the federal No Surprises Act).
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: Nueva York tiene el plazo MÁS CORTO: solo 3 años. Si su deuda médica tiene más de 3 años, es posible que ya no puedan demandarlo. NUNCA haga pagos en deudas prescritas.

NV.name: Nevada
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Nevada requires hospitals to post chargemaster prices online
Itemized bill available upon request
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
SB248 (2021) — debt collectors must send 60-day advance notice before collecting medical debt

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 4 years (open accounts / written contracts). Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline for initial billing. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: Varies by hospital. Nonprofit hospitals must provide charity care per IRS 501(r).
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.sb248_protection: SB248 (2021): Before collecting any medical debt, debt collectors MUST send a 60-day advance written notice including provider name, date of debt, amount, and statement that debt was assigned for collection.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: En Nevada, los cobradores DEBEN notificarle con 60 días de anticipación antes de intentar cobrar una deuda médica. Si no recibe esa notificación, podría ser una violación.

IL.name: Illinois
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Illinois Hospital Uninsured Patient Discount Act — uninsured patients receive substantial discounts
Community Benefits Act — nonprofit hospitals must provide charity care
Itemized bill available upon request

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 10 years (written contracts) — THE LONGEST in the U.S. Also 5 years for oral contracts. Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: Nonprofit hospitals must provide charity care per Community Benefits Act. Threshold varies (typically 200-300% FPL).
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: ILLINOIS TIENE EL PLAZO MÁS LARGO: 10 AÑOS. Esto significa que pueden demandarlo por facturas médicas de hasta una década. No asuma que una factura vieja 'ya caducó'. Siempre verifique antes de hacer pagos en deudas antiguas.

AR.name: Arkansas
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services and out-of-network care at in-network facilities
Arkansas law protects patients from surprise balance billing in emergencies and at in-network facilities
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r) — 240 days to apply from first post-discharge bill
Itemized bill available upon request — hospitals must provide clear billing information
AR.charity_care_threshold: No state minimum — varies by hospital (federal law requires nonprofit hospitals to have financial assistance policies)

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 3 years from date of service or last partial payment (AR Code 16-56-106). After 3 years, provider cannot legally collect. IMPORTANTE: cualquier pago parcial REINICIA el plazo de 3 años.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline for initial billing. Providers should bill within a reasonable time (typically 30-90 days).
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review after internal appeal denial.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: 240 days from first post-discharge bill (state law). Nonprofit hospitals cannot take extraordinary collection actions for 120 days.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill to initiate Independent Dispute Resolution under federal No Surprises Act.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Hospitals must provide itemized bill upon request with clear description of charges.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: Arkansas NO tiene ley estatal de charity care — solo aplican protecciones federales. El estatuto de limitaciones es de SOLO 3 años. NUNCA haga un pago parcial en una deuda cercana a los 3 años porque reinicia el plazo. Si el hospital es for-profit (no nonprofit), las protecciones federales de charity care NO aplican.

GA.name: Georgia
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Georgia Surprise Billing Law (GA Code 33-20E) — protects against balance billing in emergencies and at in-network facilities
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
Hospitals receiving Indigent Care Trust Fund must forgive 100% of debt for patients under 125% FPL, sliding scale 125-200% FPL
Hospitals serving low-income patients must conduct indigency screening for patients who claim they cannot pay
GA.charity_care_threshold: 125% FPL (full forgiveness, Indigent Care Trust Fund hospitals) — sliding scale 125-200% FPL
GA.key_agency: Georgia Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 6 years for written contracts. Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Insurance contracts may impose shorter deadlines.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: 240 days from first post-discharge bill (nonprofit hospitals). No deadline for Indigent Care Trust Fund hospitals.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided upon request. Hospitals must give clear, itemized statements.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: Georgia tiene un estatuto largo (6 años). Si califica para charity care via Indigent Care Trust Fund, requiere ser ciudadano y residente de GA. Consulte siempre con un profesional legal.

OH.name: Ohio
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Ohio law protects against surprise billing for emergency services and certain non-emergency out-of-network care
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
Itemized bill available upon request
OH.charity_care_threshold: No state minimum — varies by hospital. Nonprofit hospitals must follow their own financial assistance policies.

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 6 years for written contracts. Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: 240 days from first post-discharge bill for nonprofit hospitals.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided upon request. Clear, itemized statement required.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: Ohio tiene 6 años de estatuto de limitaciones pero buenas protecciones al consumidor. Pregunte siempre por el programa de asistencia financiera del hospital.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Pennsylvania Surprise Billing Law protects against balance billing in emergencies and at in-network facilities
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
PA Fair Credit Extension Uniformity Act provides consumer protections against aggressive debt collection
Itemized bill available upon request
PA.charity_care_threshold: No state minimum — varies by hospital. Nonprofit hospitals must follow their financial assistance policies.

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 4 years for written contracts. Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: 240 days from first post-discharge bill for nonprofit hospitals.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided within 30 days of request per PA law.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: PA tiene protecciones al consumidor más fuertes que el promedio. El estatuto de 4 años es razonable. Siempre solicite el programa de asistencia financiera del hospital.

NC.name: North Carolina
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
North Carolina Surprise Billing Law protects patients from balance billing in emergencies
Medical Bill De-Weaponization Act (2025) — hospitals must partner with organizations like Undue Medical Debt for patient relief
Nonprofit hospitals required to provide charity care per IRS 501(r)
Itemized bill available upon request
NC.charity_care_threshold: No state minimum — varies by hospital. State law strengthens protections against aggressive medical debt collection.

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 3 years for written contracts. Clock starts from last payment or service date. Uno de los estatutos más cortos del país.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Insurance contracts may impose shorter deadlines.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: 240 days from first post-discharge bill for nonprofit hospitals.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided upon request. Clear, itemized statement required by NC law.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: NC tiene un estatuto de SOLO 3 AÑOS — uno de los más favorables al paciente. Si su deuda tiene más de 3 años, el hospital NO puede demandarlo. NUNCA haga pagos parciales en deudas cercanas a los 3 años — reinicia el plazo.

WA.name: Washington
protections: No Surprises Act (federal) applies to emergency services
Washington Balance Billing Protection Act — comprehensive state law against surprise billing
Charity care required by STATE LAW for ALL hospitals (including for-profit) — free care under 300% FPL
Medical debt CANNOT be reported to credit agencies under WA law (2022)
Itemized bill available upon request
WA.charity_care_threshold: 300% FPL (state law — ALL hospitals, including for-profit). One of the strongest charity care laws in the U.S.
WA.key_agency: Washington State Office of the Insurance Commissioner

dispute_deadlines.statute_of_limitations: 6 years for written contracts. Clock starts from last payment or service date.
dispute_deadlines.billing_deadline: No strict state deadline. Providers should bill within a reasonable time.
dispute_deadlines.insurance_appeal: 180 days from denial for internal appeal (ACA federal requirement). 60 days for external review.
dispute_deadlines.charity_care_application: State law requires hospitals to screen patients for charity care eligibility. Application deadline varies by hospital policy.
dispute_deadlines.no_surprises_act_idr: 120 days from initial bill for Independent Dispute Resolution.
dispute_deadlines.itemized_bill: Must be provided upon request within 30 days.
dispute_deadlines.important_warning: Washington tiene una de las leyes de charity care MAS FUERTES del pais — aplica a TODOS los hospitales (no solo nonprofits) y cubre hasta 300% FPL. La deuda medica NO puede reportarse a agencias de credito. Si su ingreso es menor a 300% FPL, exija charity care.

no_surprises_act.description: Federal law effective January 1, 2022. Protects patients from surprise medical bills in emergencies and at in-network facilities.
no_surprises_act.idr_deadline: 120 days from initial bill to initiate Independent Dispute Resolution
no_surprises_act.itemized_bill: Providers must provide good-faith estimate for uninsured/self-pay patients

credit_reporting.description: As of 2023, medical debt under $500 is not reported. Debts under 1 year old are not reported. Paid medical debt is removed immediately.
credit_reporting.cfpb_rule_2025: CFPB rule (effective 2025) prohibits including medical debt on credit reports entirely — currently under legal challenge.
